recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. FHIR-14442 needs no further core source work unless PA later chooses a new model for role-specific care provider relationships beyond the existing PractitionerRole target and profiling guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-14442 said Patient.generalPractitioner was 0..* without guidance for multiple repetitions or role-specific references. Its Published/Persuasive resolution required adding PractitionerRole through FHIR-14224 and adding comments explaining why multiple GPs may be recorded and that jurisdictions can profile to 1 or 1 per type.
initial_application: GF#14442 was applied by commit 0a6deea984ef8168dae84bd73fbc994fa6d5077c, which added the multiple-GP and profiling guidance to source/patient/patient-spreadsheet.xml. The related PractitionerRole allowance was applied by GF#14224 in commit 639fc8d6894a249ee6aa560825015e77c6d767a2.
additional_context: Patient is an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini, and the current source/patient/structuredefinition-Patient.xml retains the guidance after later source refactors. The linked Zulip thread for FHIR-14224 supported adding PractitionerRole for GP-at-organization use cases. No Confluence references to FHIR-14442 or FHIR-14224, and no exact human Zulip discussion for FHIR-14442, were found.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current Patient.generalPractitioner element already includes Organization, Practitioner, and PractitionerRole target profiles, plus the requested examples for multiple GPs and the jurisdictional profiling note.
